label: Motorcycle decals
title: One kit. Print and cut layers still together.
description: Nest an irregular motorcycle graphic kit on a fixed-width vinyl roll. Keep each print element aligned with its cut path, white-ink layer and reference marks. Compare the occupied length before sending the job to the RIP.
setting: Mixed contours · free rotation · fixed roll width

label: Acrylic keyrings
title: Use the offcuts between the outlines.
description: Fit rounded and irregular keyring designs onto cast acrylic. Leave the clearance your laser and material require. Keep engraving artwork and cut outlines registered, then inspect every edge before production.
setting: Cast acrylic · engraving + cut · safety clearance

label: Sticker sets
title: Different stickers. One production sheet.
description: Arrange a mixed sticker order without reducing artwork to rectangles. Keep bleed and cut contours together; allow extra clearance for weeding and cutting. Dense placement is useful only when the finished sheet is still practical to handle.
setting: Mixed sizes · print + contour cut · bleed clearance

label: Football shirts
title: Keep the grain direction. Turn only 180°.
description: Nest the front, back and sleeve pieces of football shirts at their original size. Keep the fabric grain aligned instead of allowing arbitrary rotation. Select 180° when the material allows reversing the piece along the same axis. Use 0° for one-way prints, directional surfaces or a nap that must stay consistent.

label: Industrial parts
title: Quarter turns. Openings become usable space.
description: Use orthogonal rotation for parts that may turn by 90°. Arrange Master PRO can place a smaller part inside a usable opening in another part. The schematic also shows what happens when a packing approach treats openings as solid.

label: Product images
title: Bottles, tubes and jars. One print layout.
description: Arrange raster images of cosmetic and household-product bottles, tubes and jars on a print sheet. Keep the original image artwork while comparing the occupied area. Raster images use their bounds or a clipping mask; for contour-cut output, prepare a closed cut outline. Keep 0° for upright artwork or allow 90° when orientation is flexible.
